exposure: Plasma chitotriosidase activity (cord blood and consecutive measurements)
outcome: Neonatal morbidity (respiratory treatment, bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), patent ductus arteriosus (PDA), intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH), retinopathy of prematurity (ROP), necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC))
cohort: The study included healthy term infants (n=53), late preterm infants (33-37 gestational weeks, n=26), and very preterm infants (<=32 gestational weeks, n=35).
finding: Higher chitotriosidase activity in preterm infants was associated with invasive ventilation and the development of BPD, PDA, IVH, and ROP, suggesting a link to macrophage activation in neonatal stress and disease severity.
followup_time: Up to 36 weeks after conception for the preterm group
birth_weight: Measured, but no specific range was given as an inclusion criterion; found to positively correlate with cord blood chitotriosidase activity.
gest_age: Term, 33-37 gestational weeks (late preterm), and <=32 gestational weeks (very preterm)
